text.traditional: 妳好！我是李中明，請問妳叫什麼名字？
text.simplified: 你好！我是李中明，请问你叫什么名字？
text.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo! Wǒ shì Lǐ Zhōngmíng, qǐngwèn nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?
text.english: Hi, my name is Li Zhongming. May I ask what your name is?

text.traditional: 我姓小林，叫友美。
text.simplified: 我姓小林，叫友美。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xìng Xiǎolín, jiào Yǒuměi.
text.english: My surname is Xiaolin. My first name is Youmei.

text.traditional: 請問妳是哪國人？
text.simplified: 请问你是哪国人？
text.pinyin: Qǐngwèn nǐ shì nǎ guó rén?
text.english: May I ask where you are from?

text.traditional: 我是日本人，你呢？
text.simplified: 我是日本人，你呢？
text.pinyin: Wǒ shì Rìběn rén, nǐ ne?
text.english: I am from Japan. How about you?

text.traditional: 我是印尼人。妳喜歡台灣嗎？
text.simplified: 我是印尼人。你喜欢台湾吗？
text.pinyin: Wǒ shì Yìnní rén. Nǐ xǐhuān Táiwān ma?
text.english: I am from Indonesia. Do you like Taiwan?

text.traditional: 我喜歡台灣。
text.simplified: 我喜欢台湾。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān Táiwān.
text.english: I like Taiwan.

LESSON_ONE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Ask the same question back with 呢, without repeating the whole sentence.
LESSON_ONE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: When a question is already in the air, say the new person or thing, add 呢, and stop. 呢 repeats that question for the new person without saying the sentence again.

patternRows.english: I am Taiwanese. How about you?
Yiwen's surname is Wang. How about Zhongming?

text.traditional: A：我是日本人，你呢？ B：我是臺灣人。
text.simplified: A：我是日本人，你呢？ B：我是台湾人。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ shì Rìběn rén, nǐ ne? B: Wǒ shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: A: I am Japanese. How about you? B: I am Taiwanese.

text.traditional: A：小林小姐叫友美，李先生呢？ B：他叫中明。
text.simplified: A：小林小姐叫友美，李先生呢？ B：他叫中明。
text.pinyin: A: Xiǎolín xiǎojiě jiào Yǒuměi, Lǐ xiānsheng ne? B: Tā jiào Zhōngmíng.
text.english: A: Miss Xiaolin is called Youmei. How about Mr. Li? B: He is called Zhongming.

text.traditional: A：王太太很累，王先生呢？ B：他不累。
text.simplified: A：王太太很累，王先生呢？ B：他不累。
text.pinyin: A: Wáng tàitai hěn lèi, Wáng xiānsheng ne? B: Tā bú lèi.
text.english: A: Mrs. Wang is very tired. How about Mr. Wang? B: He is not tired.

LESSON_ONE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleTraditional: 主語 + 動詞 + 受詞
LESSON_ONE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Build a complete sentence with a subject, a verb, and an object, in that order.
LESSON_ONE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: The book's pattern keeps one order: subject, then verb, then object. The object is the person or thing the verb affects. Put 不 right before the verb to say the opposite.

text.traditional: 我喜歡李小姐，不喜歡王小姐。
text.simplified: 我喜欢李小姐，不喜欢王小姐。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān Lǐ xiǎojiě, bù xǐhuān Wáng xiǎojiě.
text.english: I like Miss Li, but I do not like Miss Wang.

examples.teachingNote: The second part does not repeat 我.

text.traditional: 你喜歡什麼？
text.simplified: 你喜欢什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān shénme?
text.english: What do you like?

examples.teachingNote: 什麼 takes the object's place when you ask what someone likes.

text.traditional: 我愛爸爸、媽媽。
text.simplified: 我爱爸爸、妈妈。
text.pinyin: Wǒ ài bàba, māma.
text.english: I love Dad and Mom.

examples.teachingNote: One verb can take two objects.

choices.label: Verb then object

choices.label: Two objects, one verb
choices.note: Both 爸爸 and 媽媽 follow the verb 愛.

choices.label: Negate the verb
choices.traditional: 我喜歡李小姐，不喜歡王小姐。
choices.simplified: 我喜欢李小姐，不喜欢王小姐。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān Lǐ xiǎojiě, bù xǐhuān Wáng xiǎojiě.
choices.english: I like Miss Li, but I do not like Miss Wang.
choices.note: Put 不 right before 喜歡.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Build the sentence in order: subject → verb → object. 不 sits right before the verb.

sentenceSpine.title: Read the pattern
sentenceSpine.description: Subject first, then the verb, then the object. Put 不 right before the verb to say you do not like someone.
notes: 不 stays right before the verb: 不喜歡.
Verbs like 喜歡 and 愛 do not take 是.

segments.hint: Put the verb of loving here.

questions.repairFeedback: 是 says what someone is; the verb 愛 takes this slot.
